speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and tell me exactly when it started relative to your fever and other symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timeline of a facial rash sparing the perioral area appearing days after fever and upper respiratory symptoms is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). Can you tell me if the facial rash had a "slapped cheek" appearance, and does the rash on her body look lacy or reticular?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic body rash is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. I am confident in this clinical diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
